items.title: A separated finite type scheme of dimension at most one with no proper one-dimensional component is affine
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a separated finite type scheme over a field of dimension at most one with no one-dimensional proper irreducible component is affine. The proof decomposes X into irreducible components, endows each with the reduced induced structure, observes that each component is either a singleton or a curve, and in the curve case uses the criterion relating proper curves to affineness of the curve (proof lines 9509-9514). The resulting map from the coproduct of the components to X is finite and surjective with affine source, and the image of an affine scheme under a finite surjective morphism is affine, which gives the conclusion (proof lines 9515-9518). H2: the reduction to the components and the descent of affineness along a finite surjection are the substance.
